---
title: "Figure 4—figure supplement 9 — score autocorrelation over the design space, for k_off and N_ch: the temporal memory that makes the naive likelihoods overconfident"
author: "Luciano Moffatt"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

<!--
THE SCORE-MEMORY MAP, the inference-level twin of supplement 8. Where supplement 8 maps the memory
left in the DATA (residual r_std), this maps the memory in the per-interval SCORE s_t = d logL / d
theta: the integral autocorrelation lag of dlogL, one scalar per parameter per cell, over the same
plane, N_ch on columns, (parameter, algorithm) on rows.

WHY THE SCORE VERSION MATTERS SEPARATELY. A biased error bar is not caused by the residual having
memory per se, it is caused by the SCORE having memory: a non-white score is exactly J_T > F_T, the
accumulated information exceeding the per-step Fisher, which IS the overconfidence Figure 4 measures.
The residual map says how much gating signal is present; this map says how much of it leaks into the
inference as correlated score, i.e. how much the reported covariance will lie. For IR they nearly
coincide (both ~1); for the naive pair the score memory runs even higher than the residual memory
(NR k_off 8.6 vs residual 5.9), because the score squares the sensitivity.

TWO PARAMETERS, opposite roles. k_off (a rate) lives in the shape of the deterministic transient;
N_ch (the count) lives in the fluctuation amplitude. Reading both shows the memory is not a single
number per algorithm but depends on what the score is sensitive to. LSE is shown for k_off only: it
fits with unitary_current fixed, so its N_ch score is pinned by assumption and not comparable (same
EXCLUDE_ROWS rule as the Figure 4 body).

MEASURED: IR ~1 for both parameters everywhere. R just above. NR 6-12. The naive-vs-recursive split is
the same story as every other panel of this figure set, here at the level of the temporal correlation
that causes it. Scale, plane and exclusion machinery shared from figure_4_common.R.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
source("figure_4_common.R")
```

```{r scale}
# Same scale as supplement 8 (the two are meant to be read together). 1 = white score, dark = memory.
LAG_LIN    <- c(1, 1.15, 1.3, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12)
LAG_BREAKS <- log10(LAG_LIN)
LAG_PAL    <- colorRampPalette(RAMP[7:13], space = "Lab")(length(LAG_LIN) - 1)
LAG_LAB    <- fmt_big(LAG_LIN)
LAG_SOL    <- 1.5
LAG_DSH    <- 3
```

```{r data}
# The score integral-lag is a MATRIX (param_index x param_col); the per-parameter memory is its
# diagonal, param_index == param_col.
lag_score <- imap_dfr(GRID_BY_ALGO, function(g, a) if (!nrow(g)) tibble() else
  pmap_dfr(g, function(nch, z) {
    read.csv(findf(nch, a, z, "battery_sim_G"), skip = 1) %>%
      filter(component_path == "Probit_statistics_Report_integral_dlogL",
             statistic == "integral_correlation_lag", probit == "mean",
             param_index == param_col, param_index %in% PIDX[PARAM_LONG]) %>%
      transmute(algo = a, noise = z, Num_ch = nch, interval_in_tau, param_index, v = value)
  })) %>%
  group_by(algo, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, param_index) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(v), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(param = names(PIDX)[match(param_index, PIDX)],
         lx = log10(interval_in_tau), ly = log10(as.numeric(noise)),
         nchf = factor(paste0("N[ch]==", Num_ch), levels = paste0("N[ch]==", NCHS)))

cat("score integral-lag by algorithm and parameter (median over grid):\n")
print(as.data.frame(lag_score %>% group_by(algo, param) %>% summarise(m = median(m), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = algo, values_from = m)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
sat(log10(lag_score$m), min(LAG_BREAKS), max(LAG_BREAKS), "score integral-lag")
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 9.5}
hC <- map_height(length(PARAM_LONG), 0.475)
g <- btitle("Score autocorrelation (integral lag of dlogL)") /
     mapblock(lag_score, function(d) log10(d$m), LAG_PAL, LAG_BREAKS, PARAM_LONG,
              top = TRUE, bottom = TRUE, iso_sol = log10(LAG_SOL), iso_dsh = log10(LAG_DSH)) /
     colorbar(LAG_PAL, LAG_LAB, "integral lag", LAG_LIN, sol = LAG_SOL, dsh = LAG_DSH)
hs <- c(0.16, hC, 0.28)
g <- g + plot_layout(heights = hs)
g
ggsave("Figure_4_supplement_9.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = sum(hs))
```
